## Before submitting

- [x] I agree to license this contribution under the terms of [LICENSE.txt](https://github.com/NVIDIA/cudnn-frontend/blob/develop/LICENSE.txt).
- [x] I ran `pre-commit run` and committed any formatting changes.
- [x] I reviewed the Hard Rules in the `AGENTS.md` for each directory this PR touches (see [root AGENTS.md § Reviewing a PR](https://github.com/NVIDIA/cudnn-frontend/blob/develop/AGENTS.md#reviewing-a-pr-human-or-agent)) and my changes comply, or I explain the exception below.
- [x] I added GitHub labels: one `cat-*`, one or more `area:*` / `op:*`, and one `orig-*` (see [label list](https://github.com/NVIDIA/cudnn-frontend/labels)).

## Affected area

C++ frontend API or graph construction.

## Summary

Fix existing Windows dynamic-loading paths to use CUDA driver and runtime DLL names, honor Python-registered DLL directories while retaining PATH and explicit-path loading, and report Windows loader errors safely. Validate Windows runtime selection while preserving existing Linux behavior. When both Windows loading attempts fail, preserve the initial `LoadLibraryExA` error instead of replacing it with the legacy fallback error. Record the native regression control in the header agent guide. Scope the Windows runtime DLL reference during validation so rejected libraries are unloaded even when error formatting throws.

## Why

Windows graph tests failed while searching for Linux CUDA library names; error reporting could also crash. Selecting CUDA 12 with CUDA 13 headers or ignoring `os.add_dll_directory()` caused additional discovery and graph API failures. If the primary and fallback searches both fail, the fallback can overwrite the diagnostic from the primary search. An allocation failure while formatting a runtime-validation error could otherwise leave the rejected DLL loaded.

## Related issues

None.

## API and compatibility impact

Windows dynamic loading requires CUDA 13 headers and a runtime reporting major 13, including explicit overrides. Additional Windows CUDA versions can be supported separately. Linux retains CUDA 12/13 discovery, first-match selection with an ambiguity warning, and existing override behavior. Static loading is unchanged.

## Testing

- Rebased onto develop `9b429bde`; retained upstream loader error checks and teardown handling. Source comparison confirmed unchanged Linux runtime selection.
- Native Windows ARM64 controls passed for registered-directory, PATH and explicit-path loading, primary-error preservation, runtime-version rejection, and exception-safe DLL ownership.
- The rebased shim passed MSVC C++17 dynamic/static compilation, native runtime/driver discovery and symbol/error checks, plus x64 compilation.
- Changed-file pre-commit checks passed. Linux execution and the broader GPU matrix were not rerun after this rebase.

* **Documentation**
  * Clarified CUDA runtime library search behavior on Linux, including how multiple matches and explicit overrides are handled.
  * Documented Windows CUDA 13 runtime requirements, library search behavior, and the need to keep Python DLL-directory handles available during discovery.

* **Bug Fixes**
  * Windows runtime loading now verifies that the selected CUDA runtime is version 13 and reports an error for incompatible runtimes.

@@ -223,22 +223,35 @@ If `import cudnn` itself fails, download [collect_env.py](python/cudnn/collect_e
 
 ### Overriding the CUDA runtime library
 
-When the frontend is built with dynamic loading enabled, it locates the CUDA runtime
-(`libcudart.so.*`) at runtime by searching for the supported major versions. In some
+On Linux, when the frontend is built with dynamic loading enabled, it locates the
+CUDA runtime (`libcudart.so.*`) by searching CUDA 12 followed by CUDA 13. In some
 environments (for example, containers such as GKE where the TCPXO NCCL plugin mounts a
 different `libcudart` major version from the host) multiple versions of `libcudart` may be
-visible on the library search path, and the automatic detection aborts with a
-`Multiple libcudart libraries found` error.
+visible on the library search path. Automatic detection warns with
+`Multiple libcudart libraries found` and keeps the first match.
 
-To resolve this, set the `CUDNN_FRONTEND_CUDART_LIB_NAME` environment variable to the
-library name (or full path) that should be loaded. This bypasses the automatic detection:
+To select a particular runtime, set `CUDNN_FRONTEND_CUDART_LIB_NAME` to the library
+name or full path. This bypasses automatic detection:
 
 ```bash
 export CUDNN_FRONTEND_CUDART_LIB_NAME=libcudart.so.13
 # or an absolute path
 export CUDNN_FRONTEND_CUDART_LIB_NAME=/usr/local/cuda/lib64/libcudart.so.13
 ```
 
+On Windows, dynamic loading currently requires CUDA 13 headers and a CUDA 13
+runtime (`cudart64_13.dll`). The loader calls `cudaRuntimeGetVersion` and rejects
+other runtime majors, including when using an explicit override. Support for
+additional Windows CUDA versions can be added separately. The loader searches
+registered DLL directories, including those added through Python's
+`os.add_dll_directory()`, and retains a PATH fallback. Keep Python DLL-directory
+handles alive for as long as library discovery may occur.
+
+```powershell
+$env:CUDNN_FRONTEND_CUDART_LIB_NAME = "cudart64_13.dll"
+# or the full path to the selected CUDA 13 runtime DLL
+```

@@ -10,6 +10,8 @@ The header-only C++ library (CMake INTERFACE target `cudnn_frontend`, C++17). Um
 - Guard anything needing a newer cuDNN with runtime `detail::get_backend_version()` checks (compare against `CUDNN_FRONTEND_VERSION`-style integers, e.g. 9.12.0 → 91200); the same headers must compile against older cuDNN 9.x. **Declare unconditionally, gate in the body**: an `#if`-conditional declaration bakes the build-time cuDNN version into the artifact, so a wheel built against 9.23 silently loses the symbol on a 9.24 system — declare the API always and return not-supported at runtime instead (review on PR #246).
 - **Guard new enum attributes with the header version, like the rest of the codebase.** Wrap the use of an attribute that only exists from cuDNN X.Y on in `#if (CUDNN_VERSION >= XY00)` with a not-supported `#else` branch, and keep the runtime backend version check (`NV_CUDNN_FE_DYNAMIC_CHECK_CUDNN_BACKEND_VERSION`) inside it. Only gate on a version whose released headers actually define the attribute; `#ifdef` cannot detect an enum constant, and guessing its integer value risks an ABI collision.
 - clang-format (Google-based, indent 4, 120 cols, `SortIncludes: false`) via `pre-commit run`.
+- Windows shim loader errors: capture `GetLastError()` immediately after the primary load fails; preserve it only if the fallback also fails, and clear errors on success. Test with primary and fallback failures that return different codes.
+- Windows runtime validation must establish scoped ownership before diagnostics can throw and transfer ownership only on success. Allocation-failure tests must verify cleanup releases exactly the validator's reference.
 - A backend correctness workaround belongs to the affected native support surface, not an unrelated frontend engine's admission. For SDPA block masks, test `AUTO` and explicit `UNIFIED`, runtime versions below/at the fix, and unaffected architectures/no-mask controls. Mask contents are mutable device data; an all-visible validation sample cannot establish a safe reusable plan. `SDPA block-mask backend support boundary` is the descriptor-only detector; actual numerical qualification must identify the loaded released backend artifact, not just its version label.
